head: Who’s in net for the Oilers?
paras: The Islanders have won two in a row, and the Oilers (9-2-2) beat Calgary 4-0 on Wednesday. Going in, the Oilers are first in the Pacific (third in the NHL) and the Islanders fourth in the Metropolitan (tied for tenth).

The Oilers’ record (.769) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.622), largely thanks to their finishing. So is the Islanders’ (.615 on chances worth .521), largely thanks to their goaltending.

Both teams get their defensemen shooting. The Oilers lean on their stars more than any team in the league. No team gives its bottom six less of the ice time. The Islanders, by contrast, spread the ice time through the lineup (3rd). The Oilers also have the league’s most dangerous power play, and that could do real damage when the Islanders are shorthanded, though the Islanders’ penalty killers create chances of their own going the other way. Edmonton has scored 4.23 goals a game, the most in the league. On the other side, the Islanders have had some of the league’s best goaltending. Both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Connor McDavid (8 G / 28 A / 36 P in 13 GP) leads the Oilers and the whole NHL in scoring, with 13 points in his last five games. Leon Draisaitl (12 G / 12 A / 24 P in 13 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, second in the NHL, with ten points in his last five games and seven goals in six games against the Islanders since 2023-24. Bo Horvat (7 G / 7 A / 14 P in 13 GP) is tied for the Isles’ scoring lead. Matthew Schaefer (4 G / 10 A / 14 P in 13 GP) shares it, with seven points in his last five games.

Tristan Jarry (3-1-2 / .883 SV% in 6 GS) is in line to start for Edmonton. Ilya Sorokin (6-3-0 / .915 SV% in 9 GS) has been outstanding for the Islanders and will likely start. Sorokin has a .943 save percentage in five starts against the Oilers, well above his usual .906. Don’t read much into it: a goalie’s record against one team rarely holds up.

items.text: The Oilers are newly without Zach Hyman, and have had to make do without Matt Savoie all season.

The Islanders have been without Matias Maccelli since Oct 17, and have had to make do without Mathew Barzal all season. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Maple Leafs are missing more right now.
Connor McDavid has a point in every game this season.
Evan Bouchard has seven goals on chances worth about 2.8 goals, well above what his finishing usually turns chances into. Runs like that tend to cool off.

NYI.head: The Islanders start a half-step behind
NYI.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately, while the Islanders will be without Barzal. Then again, Edmonton will be without Hyman, and the Islanders have home-ice advantage. The Islanders can tip it if they keep shots to a minimum.

EDM.head: Leaning the Oilers’ way
EDM.body: Edmonton has been out-chancing opponents lately, while the Islanders will be without Barzal. Then again, Edmonton will be without Hyman, and the Islanders have home-ice advantage. The Islanders can still swing it if they keep shots to a minimum.

calls.head: Sorokin doesn’t own the Oilers
calls.body: Sorokin has been a wall against the Oilers since 2023-24, well above his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if Sorokin isn’t that wall tonight.

calls.head: Special teams lean toward the Oilers
calls.body: The Islanders’ penalty kill is one of the league’s worst, and the Oilers’ power play is the best. Discipline matters more than usual for the Islanders tonight. Edmonton has had one of the league’s most effective power plays for years.

calls.head: Keep your head up
calls.body: The Oilers and the Islanders are both among the league’s heaviest hitters, even after adjusting for each arena’s scorer. Keep your head up.

calls.head: Strength in numbers for the Islanders
calls.body: The Islanders roll four lines, but the Oilers lean on their top six. The Islanders are one of the league’s best for depth, and Edmonton is the worst. They’re about as far apart as two teams get. If this one comes down to the bottom six, that suits the Islanders.
